description: Interactive 3D Earth globe at /map that visualizes photo locations using GPS metadata with thumbnail markers, clustering, and group navigation

userStories.title: Install Three.js ecosystem dependencies
userStories.description: As a developer, I need three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, and r3f-globe installed so we can build the globe component.
acceptanceCriteria: Run: npm install three @react-three/fiber @react-three/drei r3f-globe
@react-three/fiber is v9+ (React 19 compatible)
@react-three/drei is v10+
r3f-globe is v1.6+
npm run type-check passes with new dependencies
npm run build succeeds (no SSR issues)

userStories.title: Create GET /api/media/geo endpoint
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an API route that returns all geo-tagged media across the user's groups so the globe can display them.
acceptanceCriteria: New file at src/app/api/media/geo/route.ts with GET handler
Uses createServerComponentClient() for auth (respects RLS)
Queries media_assets WHERE latitude IS NOT NULL AND longitude IS NOT NULL
Joins with groups table to include group name
Only returns media from groups the authenticated user is a member of
Response shape: { points: Array<{ id, groupId, groupName, lat, lng, thumbnailKey, filename, locationCountry, locationCity }> }
Selects only required columns (id, group_id, latitude, longitude, thumbnail_key, filename, location_country, location_city)
Returns 401 if user is not authenticated
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Response uses 'lat'/'lng' field names to match r3f-globe's default htmlLat/htmlLng accessors

userStories.title: Create useGeoMedia hook
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a client-side hook that fetches the geo endpoint and caches the result for the globe component to consume.
acceptanceCriteria: New file at src/presentation/hooks/use-geo-media.ts
Hook calls GET /api/media/geo on mount
Returns { points, loading, error, refresh }
Caches result in state (does not refetch on re-render)
Handles error state (fetch failure, 401)
Exports GeoPoint type: { id: string, groupId: string, groupName: string, lat: number, lng: number, thumbnailKey: string, filename: string, locationCountry?: string, locationCity?: string }
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: GeoPoint uses 'lat'/'lng' to match r3f-globe's default htmlLat/htmlLng accessors

userStories.title: Create /map route page with dynamic import shell
userStories.description: As a user, I want to access the globe view from the dashboard navigation at /map.
acceptanceCriteria: New file at src/app/(dashboard)/map/page.tsx inside the existing dashboard route group
Page has 'use client' directive
Globe component is imported via next/dynamic with { ssr: false }
Shows a centered loading spinner/skeleton while the globe component loads
The dynamic import points to a placeholder component at src/presentation/components/globe/photo-globe.tsx (can be a simple div for now)
Add a 'Map' link to the dashboard nav bar in src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx next to existing links
Globe container fills viewport height minus nav bar (h-[calc(100dvh-64px)] or equivalent)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Create geo-utils with clustering logic
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a utility function to cluster nearby geo points so the globe isn't cluttered with overlapping markers.
acceptanceCriteria: New file at src/presentation/components/globe/geo-utils.ts
Export function clusterPoints(points: GeoPoint[], distanceThresholdKm: number): Array<{ center: { lat: number, lng: number }, points: GeoPoint[] }> that groups nearby points
Clustering uses haversine distance formula for geographic accuracy
Default distance threshold is configurable (suggest 50km)
Single points (no neighbors within threshold) become clusters of size 1
Cluster center is the average lat/lng of its members
Export haversineDistance(lat1, lng1, lat2, lng2) helper for reuse
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: latLngToVector3 is NOT needed — r3f-globe's HTML Elements Layer handles lat/lng to 3D positioning natively

userStories.title: Render Earth globe with R3F Canvas and r3f-globe
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the base 3D scene with an Earth globe rendered inside the photo-globe component.
acceptanceCriteria: Update src/presentation/components/globe/photo-globe.tsx to render an R3F <Canvas>
Canvas has dark background (matching app theme, e.g. #0a0a0a)
r3f-globe component renders inside the Canvas with earth-day or earth-night texture
Globe has atmospheric glow effect (r3f-globe atmosphereColor and atmosphereAltitude props)
OrbitControls from drei: rotation enabled, zoom enabled (minDistance and maxDistance set), pan disabled (enablePan={false})
Auto-rotate enabled by default (autoRotate={true}, autoRotateSpeed={0.5})
Camera positioned at a distance that shows the full globe on load
Globe fills its container div completely
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Render photo thumbnail markers using r3f-globe HTML Elements Layer
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my photo thumbnails floating on the globe at the locations where they were taken, using r3f-globe's built-in HTML Elements Layer for positioning and occlusion.
acceptanceCriteria: New file at src/presentation/components/globe/create-marker-element.ts — a function that creates a DOM element for a single marker
photo-globe.tsx uses useGeoMedia() to fetch geo points
Uses useUrlCache from existing hooks to get presigned thumbnail URLs for each point's thumbnailKey
Pass clustered data to r3f-globe via htmlElementsData prop
Use htmlLat='lat' and htmlLng='lng' accessors (matching GeoPoint field names)
Set htmlAltitude={0.01} to lift markers slightly above globe surface
htmlElement accessor calls createMarkerElement() which returns a DOM element via document.createElement()
Each marker DOM element is a 40px circular div with overflow:hidden, border-radius:50%, white 2px border, containing an with the thumbnail URL
htmlElementVisibilityModifier toggles opacity to 0/1 for occlusion (hiding markers behind the globe)
htmlTransitionDuration={500} for smooth position transitions
Cursor set to pointer on marker elements via CSS
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Using r3f-globe's native HTML Elements Layer (htmlElementsData, htmlElement, htmlLat, htmlLng, htmlElementVisibilityModifier) instead of drei <Html>. This handles lat/lng positioning, occlusion, and transitions natively. Trade-off: markers are imperative DOM elements (document.createElement), not React JSX.

userStories.title: Implement thumbnail stacking for clustered markers
userStories.description: As a user, I want nearby photos to stack together so the globe isn't cluttered, with a count badge showing how many photos are in each stack.
acceptanceCriteria: photo-globe.tsx uses clusterPoints() from geo-utils to group nearby points before passing to htmlElementsData
Each cluster becomes one entry in htmlElementsData with center lat/lng and its array of points
createMarkerElement handles both single-point and multi-point clusters
Clusters of 1: single circular thumbnail (40px)
Clusters of 2+: overlapping circular thumbnails (max 3 visible, offset by 8px each) built as nested DOM elements
Clusters with more than 3 photos show a '+N' count badge (small pill div, positioned at top-right of the stack)
Stack thumbnails have box-shadow for depth effect
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Cluster data shape passed to htmlElementsData: { lat, lng, points: GeoPoint[], thumbnailUrls: string[] }

userStories.title: Add fan-out animation on cluster hover
userStories.description: As a user, I want to hover over a stacked cluster and see the individual photos fan out so I can see each one.
acceptanceCriteria: On mouseenter over a cluster DOM element, child thumbnail divs animate from stacked position to a circular fan-out arrangement via CSS transitions
Fan-out shows up to 8 thumbnails positioned in a circle (using transform: translate + rotate)
If more than 8 photos in cluster, show first 7 + a '+N more' text indicator
On mouseleave, thumbnails animate back to stacked position
Animation uses CSS transitions on transform + opacity (200ms ease-out)
Each fanned-out thumbnail has its own click handler (set via onclick on the DOM element)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: All animation is pure CSS transitions on DOM elements created in createMarkerElement. No React state needed — toggle a CSS class on mouseenter/mouseleave.

userStories.title: Click marker/cluster to navigate to group
userStories.description: As a user, I want to click a photo marker to navigate to the group containing that photo.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a single marker navigates to /groups/{groupId}
Clicking a fanned-out thumbnail navigates to that photo's group
Clicking a stacked (not fanned) cluster: if all photos are from the same group, navigate directly; if mixed groups, fan out first
Navigation uses window.location.href or a callback passed into createMarkerElement (since markers are imperative DOM, not React components)
Navigation does not conflict with OrbitControls (click vs drag detection — use pointer-events:auto on markers and stopPropagation)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Since markers are DOM elements outside React, navigation can use window.location.href='/groups/{id}' or accept a callback from the parent component

userStories.title: Add location labels using r3f-globe Labels Layer
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see country/city names near photo clusters for geographic context.
acceptanceCriteria: Use r3f-globe's built-in Labels Layer (labelsData, labelLat, labelLng, labelText props) instead of custom HTML elements
Build labels array from cluster data: one label per cluster using locationCity or locationCountry
Deduplicate labels: if multiple clusters share the same label text and are nearby, only include one
labelColor set to semi-transparent white (rgba(255,255,255,0.6))
labelSize set to 0.4 (subtle, not overwhelming)
labelAltitude set to 0.015 (slightly above markers)
labelDotRadius set to 0 (no dot marker, just text)
labelsTransitionDuration={500} for smooth transitions
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Using r3f-globe's native Labels Layer rather than HTML elements for labels. This renders labels as 3D text on the globe surface, which looks more integrated.

userStories.title: Add animated transitions and visual polish
userStories.description: As a user, I want the globe experience to feel smooth and polished with entrance animations and idle auto-rotation.
acceptanceCriteria: Globe fades in on initial load (opacity 0 to 1 over 500ms on the container div)
Markers animate in via htmlTransitionDuration — they transition from altitude 0 to their target altitude for a 'pop-up' entrance effect
Auto-rotate pauses when user interacts (drag/zoom), resumes after 3 seconds of idle
Overall performance: smooth 60fps with up to 500 markers (verified by keeping DOM nodes low via clustering)
Empty state: if no geo-tagged photos exist, show a message 'No photos with location data yet' centered on the page instead of the globe
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Leverage htmlTransitionDuration and htmlElementVisibilityModifier for marker animations rather than custom JS animation code
